Critical SCALE/CAMERA correction: the current background has giant foreground furniture and a high camera and makes the overlaid adult NPC look tiny. Change to LOW CHARACTER EYE LEVEL camera, height about 1.0m, subtle upward architectural lens shift, horizon/vanishing point around 65% canvas height. Pull all shelves, the checkout desk and produce fixtures into the back half of the room, REDUCE their projected dimensions about 35% vs reference, leaving a usable walking area from y72% to the bottom. A composited adult character will stand x55% feet y89% and be about 30% of frame HEIGHT: countertop should be near waist height for that character, not above its head, door height ~35-40% of frame, chairs if any ~16% of frame. Practical modest room, no enormous hangar. Keep an intimate scene with fewer distant objects, clear medium-sized details, not an ultra-wide giant room. Perspective should visually suit an adult at those positions. Preserve village geography visible outside. Photorealistic natural daylight, crisp wide 16:9, straight verticals, no blurry upscaling. No characters, people, animals, silhouettes, NPCs, text, labels, signs or UI. No drawn scale guides or rulers.
